narrative:
The model has flagged you as needing remedial courses, but its estimated probability of failing is 15%, meaning it sees an 85% chance you pass. That is a low fail risk, not a certainty; the remedial requirement should be read as a precautionary support decision based on the model’s risk flag, not a statement that failure is likely.

The strongest factor in your prediction was your reason for choosing the school: choosing it for its reputation pushed your estimated risk downward, toward passing. Second was your record of past class failures: you have none, which also worked in your favor. Third was the quality of your family relationships: you report good relationships, and about 62% of passing students also report good family relationships. These top three signals were protective—they lowered your estimated fail risk and help explain why it is only 15% rather than much higher. The remaining risk reflects the combined effect of smaller factors, so the model still treats support as necessary.

To improve your position, keep your attendance strong, since you currently report no absences. Continue your weekly study routine of two to five hours and use the family educational support you already have. Maintain the good family relationships that are helping you, and ask whether school-based support or paid tutoring is available if you want extra help.
